ops-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 ALERT: continuous-batcher p99 > 3.0s over 10m in us-west-2. Auto-page to #eng-oncall. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/contbatch?from=-15m

Priya (SRE): pinging oncall. I'm looking at tail histograms and streaming request logs. p95 ~1.2s, p99 ~3.6s. Spike started ~6167890000.

Ken (Runtime): noticed a sudden increase in large-seq requests interleaved with very short seqs. The packer is grouping them -> big batches -> KV lookups + paging. Streaming connections show long stall durations (200-1k ms). No recent runtime deploys.

Priya (SRE): any quick toggles to improve latency without risky deploys?

Ken (Runtime): yes, small set of runtime flags we can flip via control plane:
1) lower contbatch.max_batch_size 48 -> 24
2) enable fast_path_short_seqs (sequence bucketing) to prioritize tiny sequences
3) enable stream_isolation:true so streaming requests use separate pack window
Commands:
```bash
redctl pool update contbatch --set max_batch_size=24
redctl pool update contbatch --set fast_path_short_seqs=true
redctl pool update contbatch --set stream_isolation=true
```

Priya (SRE): applying change 1 now. `redctl` returned ok. Watching telemetry.

(20s)
Priya (SRE): After batch size cap -> p99 dropped from 3.6s -> 2.4s. Streaming stall rate down ~25%.

Ken (Runtime): apply 2) sequence bucketing now. Low risk.

Priya (SRE): applied fast_path_short_seqs=true.

(40s)
Priya (SRE): p99 trending to ~1.5s, p95 steady. Streaming stalls nearly back to baseline.

Dana (PM): Customer impact? any active customer pages?

Victor (Support): We've got 2 enterprise alerts: INC-9012 (partial streaming) and INC-9013 (slow responses). Both reporting increased latency since ~10m ago. No dropped responses. Customers asking for ETA and root cause.

Priya (SRE): Recommend short public status: "We observed increased tail latency due to mixed sequence length batching causing oversized batches and cache churn. Mitigation applied (batch cap + bucketing). Service recovering; engineering investigating root cause and follow-up fixes." ETA for follow-up: 1.5 hours.

Victor (Support): I'll post that and update tickets. Clarify no data loss.

Ken (Runtime): For long-term fixes we should:
- implement per-seqlen admission + preemptive slice of long sequences
- adaptive batching: lower max_batch_size automatically when seqlen variance high
- streaming fallback pool to keep streams latency-sensitive
- KV cache async eviction + background warming to avoid blocking paths
I'll file tech tasks.

Rami (Eng): I'll own the adaptive batching PoC. Creating ticket RW-5201 and linking metrics. PR target: 5 business days for prototype.

Priya (SRE): ops note: do not auto-revert these runtime flags. Manual review required before rollback. Documented the changes and timestamps.

ops-bot: Incident state -> Mitigated. Paging suspended.

Priya (SRE): summary timestamps: incident start ~6167890000, mitigations applied ~6167890185, p99 pre-incident baseline ~0.8s, peak ~3.6s, post-mitigation ~1.4s and stable for 5m.

Victor (Support): customer messages sent. Tickets updated.

Rami (Eng): Handoff: I'll pick up follow-up engineering work (RW-5201). Will post design notes and perf tests here. ETA for design doc: 48h.

Dana (PM): scheduling a 30m post-incident sync in 1h to review mitigations and customer comms.

Priya (SRE): handing oncall to Rami for ongoing monitoring for next 6h. Link to runbook: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/contbatch-tail

Ken (Runtime): I'll add flame graphs + sample traces to RW-5201. Will also add a canary detector for seqlen variance that triggers auto-lowering of max_batch_size as a safety net.

Priya (SRE): good work team. :thumbsup:

Rami (Eng): acknowledged. ping me for anything urgent.

ops-bot: Thread archived after mitigation update.
